subject.title: [Bug]: Critical Data Loss Due to Silent Daily Session Reset (No user warning, no opt-out discovery) #42100

question: What should OpenClaw's default session reset lifecycle guarantee for existing and new users: keep daily rollover as the default with clearer warnings, switch to manual/longer-lived continuity by default, or add a staged admin-controlled migration path?
rationale: The remaining work changes public reset semantics, config schema, channel UX, archive recovery, and upgrade behavior; source inspection confirms the code path is real, but automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a reset lifecycle design
options.body: Define the default policy, manual-only/config shape, setup/docs visibility, warning/postpone behavior, restore/readback path, and migration rules before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to manual-only config first
options.body: Land only the explicit never/manual reset mode and keep warning, restore, and admin-policy work tracked separately, accepting that this issue stays partially unresolved.

options.title: Keep daily default as policy
options.body: Close or narrow the broad request only if maintainers intentionally want daily rollover to remain the primary default and accept the documented continuity tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a reset lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Define the default policy, manual-only/config shape, setup/docs visibility, warning/postpone behavior, restore/readback path, and migration rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the daily reset policy and was explicitly asked in the issue discussion to help decide the reset lifecycle direction.
